content: This document provides a summary of information about the medication flibanserin but does not include all possible details. It does not guarantee that the medication is safe, effective, or appropriate for you. This information is not a substitute for personalized medical advice. Always consult your healthcare provider for complete information about this medication and your specific health needs. Warning: Consuming alcohol close to the time you take flibanserin significantly increases the risk of severe low blood pressure and fainting. If you consume one or two alcoholic drinks in the evening, you must wait at least two hours before taking flibanserin at bedtime. After taking flibanserin at bedtime, do not consume any alcohol until the following day. If you consume three or more alcoholic drinks in the evening, you should skip your dose of flibanserin that night. Do not take flibanserin if you have liver problems or if you are taking certain medications that may interact with it, as this increases the risk of severe low blood pressure or fainting. Refer to the Drug Interactions section for more details. Before starting flibanserin, inform your doctor and pharmacist if you have liver problems and provide a list of all products you use, including prescription drugs, non-prescription drugs, and herbal products. Flibanserin is not intended to treat low sexual desire caused by medical or mental/mood disorders, relationship problems, or the effects of other drugs. It should not be used by women who have gone through menopause or by men. How to Use: Read the Medication Guide provided by your pharmacist before starting flibanserin and each time you get a refill. Take this medication by mouth as directed by your doctor, usually once daily at bedtime. Taking flibanserin only at bedtime reduces the risk of low blood pressure, fainting, and drowsiness while awake. After taking flibanserin, avoid consuming alcohol until the next day. Avoid eating grapefruit or drinking grapefruit juice while using this medication unless your doctor or pharmacist advises otherwise, as grapefruit can increase the likelihood of side effects. Take this medication regularly to achieve the most benefit. Common side effects may include drowsiness, dizziness, nausea, or tiredness. Remember that this medication has been prescribed because your doctor has determined that the benefits outweigh the risks of side effects. Low blood pressure and fainting may occur even if you take flibanserin alone. The risk of these side effects is higher if you take the medication with alcohol, less than two hours after alcohol, at a time other than bedtime, or in doses higher than prescribed. If you feel dizzy or lightheaded, lie down immediately. Serious allergic reactions to this drug are rare. This is not a complete list of possible side effects. In the U.S., contact your doctor for medical advice about side effects. In Canada, consult your doctor for medical advice about side effects. Precautions: Before taking flibanserin, inform your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to it or if you have any other allergies. This product may contain inactive ingredients that can cause allergic reactions or other problems. This drug may cause dizziness or drowsiness. Alcohol or marijuana (cannabis) can exacerbate these effects. Do not drive, use machinery, or perform tasks requiring alertness for at least six hours after taking flibanserin and until you can do so safely. Avoid alcoholic beverages. During pregnancy, this medication should only be used when clearly needed. It is unknown if this medication passes into breast milk. Due to potential risks to the infant, breastfeeding is not recommended while using this medication. Drug Interactions: Drug interactions may alter how your medications work or increase your risk of serious side effects. This document does not include all possible drug interactions. Keep a list of all the products you use (including prescription/non-prescription drugs and herbal products) and share it with your doctor and pharmacist. Other medications can affect the removal of flibanserin from your body, potentially altering its effectiveness. Examples include azole antifungals (e.g., fluconazole, ketoconazole), certain calcium channel blockers (e.g., diltiazem, verapamil), macrolide antibiotics (e.g., clarithromycin, erythromycin), nefazodone, rifamycins (e.g., rifabutin, rifampin), ritonavir, and St. John’s wort. Check the labels on all your medications (e.g., allergy or cough-and-cold products) as they may contain ingredients that cause drowsiness. Overdose: If someone has overdosed and exhibits serious symptoms such as passing out or difficulty breathing, call 911 immediately. Otherwise, contact a poison control center right away. U.S. residents can call 1-800-222-1222. Canadian residents can call 1-844-764-7669. Missed Dose: If you miss a dose, skip the missed dose. Take your next dose at bedtime the following day. Storage: Store at room temperature away from light and moisture. Do not store in the bathroom. Do not flush medications down the toilet or pour them into a drain unless instructed to do so. Properly discard this product when it is expired or no longer needed. Important: This information is a summary and does not include all possible details about this product. It does not guarantee that the product is safe, effective, or appropriate for you. Always consult your healthcare provider for complete information about this product and your specific health needs.
